title: Follow-up: PositionsGlanceTable's price formatting silently gained thousands separators (PR #81)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #81 (frontend-dashboard-page-followups), tracked so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: PR #81 switched PositionsGlanceTable.tsx from its own inline `formatNullableCurrency` (`value === null/undefined ? '—' : \`$${value.toFixed(2)}\``, no thousands separator) onto the new shared `utils/format.ts` `formatNullableCurrency`, which wraps `formatCurrency`'s `toLocaleString(..., {style:'currency', ...})`. For any price at or above $1,000 (a plausible `current_price`/`avg_cost_basis` for many real tickers), the rendered text on the Dashboard's positions-at-a-glance table now differs from before the consolidation — e.g. `$1234.50` before vs `$1,234.50` after — gaining a thousands separator it previously lacked. This is consistent with the precedent already established in frontend-portfolio-risk-panel-followups (PR #77's `decisions` entry: the richer `toLocaleString` formatting is 'strictly better, never worse' for a finance app, so standardizing on it is intentional and desirable, not a bug), but two gaps are worth closing: (1) PositionsGlanceTable.test.tsx's only priced fixture is $228.90 (see `aaplPosition.current_price`), so no test exercises a 4-digit price and would catch a future regression in this formatting; (2) this PR's own `decisions` entry frames the PositionsGlanceTable/PositionsTable fold-in purely as consolidating null-check logic and doesn't explicitly call out that the numeric formatting itself changes for 4+-digit prices at this specific call site. Consider adding a >=$1,000 price fixture/assertion to PositionsGlanceTable.test.tsx, and noting the intentional formatting-output change explicitly in a future decision record for full traceability.

decisions.decision: Added a >=$1,000-price fixture (`highPricedPosition`, `current_price: 1234.5`) to PositionsGlanceTable.test.tsx with an assertion that it renders as `$1,234.50` (thousands separator present), alongside the existing $228.90 fixture. Also extended `formatNullableCurrency`'s file-header comment in utils/format.ts to explicitly state that PositionsGlanceTable.tsx's rendered output changes for 4+-digit prices (old `$${value.toFixed(2)}` had no thousands separator; the new shared helper does), rather than only implying it via the general formatCurrency-is-strictly-better rationale already present.
decisions.rationale: PR #81's review already correctly identified and accepted this as an intentional, desirable change (matching the PR #77 precedent), not a bug — so the fix here is purely closing the two traceability gaps the review flagged, not reconsidering the formatting choice itself. A new fixture at exactly $1,000+ (chosen as 1234.50, a plausible real per-share price, e.g. BRK.A-style) is the minimal regression test that would have caught this specific change before it shipped, given the existing suite's only priced fixture was $228.90 (3 digits, no separator to lose). Rejected changing the existing $228.90 fixture's value instead of adding a new one: that would remove test coverage for the 3-digit case while gaining 4-digit coverage, when both are worth asserting independently since they exercise different `toLocaleString` formatting paths. Rejected only updating the code comment without adding a test (or vice versa): the checklist item explicitly asks for both a fixture/assertion and a decision record, and the two gaps are independent (one is runtime regression protection, the other is documentation for future readers of utils/format.ts), so both were done.
